The Battle of Qaradagh was a military engagement fought between the two Kurdish principalities of Baban and Ardalan, supported by Qajar Iran. During the 1780’s, Baban revolted against influence of both the Ottoman Empire and Qajar Iran, making significant progress in the north. Due to their successes against the two powers, Baban would attempt to exert its influence over the regional Kurdish states, ordering the various Kurdish states to pay tribute, with Ardalan being the only state to defy them. This insubordination led to an invasion of Ardalan by Baban, but they were invaded for a secondary reason as well. Since Ardalan was a Qajar ally in the region, Baban saw this as an opportunity to throw Qajar Iran out of the region for good. Due to the military disparity between the two states, Ardalan asked Qajar Iran for military aid, to which they readily agreed. After a long battle, the Qajar-Ardalani force was defeated, forcing the withdrawal of the enemy to Persia proper. This battle would indirectly influence the organization and strength of the Babani army, arming themselves with European firearms and cavalry, becoming a regional power in the region.

The Battle
The Babanese force, made primarily of armored cavalry, crashed into the lines of the Qajar-Ardalani force, from which a brutal melee erupted. After hours of fighting, the Babanese force began to lose heart. Seeing this, Emir Muhammad Pasha charged into the front lines, galvanizing his men and strengthening their collective resolve to keep fighting. With the Babanese forces determined to break the stalemate, they pushed the Qajar-Ardalani force back onto the hill on which Qaradagh was placed. After further fighting, the Qajar-Ardalani force began to withdraw, due to them suffering grievous casualties.
